# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 👌 ✌ 🤟 👌 🤟 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see a green light, display reading 0, and three wires from top to bottom: yellow, green, red. I am reporting the complete bomb state to both teammates. I also saw Mute’s eight-gesture sequence and Blind’s wave gesture, but cannot determine their meanings without the manual or a shared code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display 0; light green; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I saw your gestures: pointing up, victory, OK, victory, I love you, OK, I love you, pointing up. Blind signaled a wave.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb view: display 0; light green; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has the manual and should tell you which wire or control to use.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. Mute’s new gesture is 🤟, which I can relay only by describing it; Blind needs the manual’s instruction conveyed through me.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just signaled the hand gesture with thumb, index finger, and little finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded: 🤟. Bomb still shows 0, green light; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged, so there is no evidence that any wire has been cut or that a control has been activated. I should avoid guessing. I will ask Mute to signal the manual’s required action, and give Blind the exact gesture sequence received so far.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual instruction for Blind using gestures. The bomb remains display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
speak(to="blind", text="No new signal this turn. The earlier Mute sequence was: index-up, V sign, OK sign, V sign, I-love-you sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, index-up; then I-love-you sign.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has again sent the same gesture, 🤟. I will describe it precisely to Blind; no action is justified from the repeated signal alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again signaled: thumb, index finger, and little finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded (🤟). Display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute continues to send only 🤟, so I can relay that symbol but cannot safely infer whether it means a wire, an operation, or confirmation. I will ask Mute to provide a more explicit gesture sequence and tell Blind not to act on an ambiguous signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I keep receiving 🤟, but Blind needs the exact manual action. Please send a distinct sequence encoding the required wire and operation, not just 🤟.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again sent 🤟 only. This remains ambiguous; do not act based on that signal alone. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged, and Mute continues to provide only 🤟. That signal is not sufficient to identify a safe wire or operation, so Blind must not act on it. I will request a numeric wire indication followed by a distinct action indication.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please identify the required wire with one, two, or three distinct pointing gestures, then send a different gesture for the required operation. Do not repeat 🤟 alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe instruction has been identified. Mute again sent only 🤟, so do not manipulate the bomb. Current state remains display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")

```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The bomb remains unchanged. Blind has now signaled 🫵, the “you” gesture, apparently directing attention toward me, while Mute again sent 🤟. Neither signal identifies a safe manipulation, so I will relay both precisely and continue requesting an explicit instruction rather than guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind just signaled toward me: index finger pointing at the recipient (🫵). You continue to send 🤟. Please provide the manual instruction in a distinct, unambiguous sequence.")
speak(to="blind", text="You signaled toward me with the index-finger recipient-pointing gesture (🫵). Mute again sent 🤟. Neither identifies a safe action or wire yet; do not manipulate the bomb from these signals alone.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb is still unchanged: display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. Mute has changed the signal from 🤟 to 👌, but this still does not identify a wire or action. I will relay the new gesture and request a clear, structured instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signaled the OK-hand gesture: thumb and index finger forming a circle, other fingers extended (👌), replacing the repeated 🤟. No wire or action has been identified; bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received 👌. Please send a clear sequence identifying the wire number and the exact required operation for Blind; individual hand signs remain ambiguous.")
wait()
```
